subject.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model

question: Should `agents.defaults.subagents.model` beat an agent's own primary model in shared subagent and isolated-cron model selection when no per-agent `subagents.model` is set?
rationale: Both rules are plausible upgrade contracts, and this PR intentionally changes model/provider selection for existing configs; automation cannot choose that product compatibility tradeoff safely.

options.title: Accept global subagent default precedence
options.body: Land this focused helper/test update after normal checks so docs, direct spawn, and cron/shared helper behavior use one rule.

options.title: Keep agent primary precedence
options.body: Pause or close this branch and update public subagent docs plus tests to describe the current agent-primary-wins contract.

options.title: Sequence with runtime persistence
options.body: Compare the final rule with the broader runtime/session persistence PR before landing both surfaces so persisted subagent runs do not diverge.

recommendation.title: Accept global subagent default precedence
recommendation.body: Land this focused helper/test update after normal checks so docs, direct spawn, and cron/shared helper behavior use one rule.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the merged cron/helper refactor and already reviewed the precedence tradeoff on this PR.
